thread:
Oncall Bot: HIGH severity alert: NLB target health flapping in euc2-azb — 5xx surge + client retries detected. auto-pager: @oncall
Maria K: I’m on call. seeing a bunch of 502/504 spikes in the dashboard, latency up 3-4x for some customers. paging now. :rotating_light:
Eli R: joining. any origin change/deploys in last 10m? @maria
Maria K: no deploys. nothing on changelog. traces show retries from multiple edge IPs hitting identical backend targets (dup path). looks like requests being routed twice across AZ boundary.
Nguyen T: I’m seeing connection resets on envoy logs in euc2-azb. log snippet:
```
[envoy][2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] upstream reset: connection failure, reason: ECONNRESET, attempt=1, host=10.2.45.12:8080
[lb][2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] healthcheck: unhealthy targets: 4/6
```
Ashok P: NLB metrics show high TargetResponseTime and RetryCount spike. Could be path duplication at the NLB->envoy layer (route table/tunneling duplication).
SRE Pager: customer-facing impact: about 18% p50 p99 latency regression for affected tenants in eu-central region. Some POSTs failing with 502/504. partial outage for euc2-azb customers.
Maria K: ok mitigation plan — immediate: mark euc2-azb target group as draining, shift traffic to euc2-aze/euc2-aza. create failover routing in Route53 while we debug.
Eli R: agree. I'll initiate weighted routing change. @deploy-bot can you apply a temporary weight shift to reduce euc2-azb to 5%?
Deploy Bot: Executing Route53 weighted-reroute: change-id=chg-9087
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3XXXX --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc2-azb","Weight":5,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZNLB","DNSName":"nlb-euc2-azb"}}}]}'
```
Deploy Bot: Route53 change submitted, status: PENDING. expected TTL effect ~30s-2m.
Nguyen T: while routing shifts, we should also remove half of NLB targets in azb to stop duplicate hits. I’m running deregister on targetgroup tg-azb-1 now.
Maria K: do it. also flip healthcheck tuning to be slightly more aggressive to avoid flapping re-registration (increase healthy threshold to 3 -> 5?).
Nguyen T: deregister command:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg-azb-1 --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e
```
Nguyen T: deregistration in progress, connection resets drop in envoy tail — seeing fewer ECONNRESET lines.
Eli R: Route53 weights showing drift, traffic to azb down to ~7% within 45s. backend error rate decreasing slowly.
Ashok P: quick root cause hypothesis: duplicate eBPF iptables rules from a recent infra change created mirrored path across a cross-AZ router, causing two NLB path hits and connection resets when backend closed old socket.
Maria K: can infra confirm an eBPF rollout in the past hour? @Ashok @Nguyen
Ashok P: I see a canary canary-rollout of conntrack eBPF rule at 09:06 across euc2. the canary targeted azb and aze but a misflag caused azb to receive an older rule plus new one — path duplication. filing bug.
SRE Pager: customer impact update: error budget burn increased; about 20% of API calls for eu customers returned 502 in last 10m. major customers report increased latency but core functionality mostly degraded not fully down.
Maria K: next steps: 1) keep azb drained 2) rollback eBPF change for azb (Nguyen/Ashok) 3) continue weight shift to 0% until rollback confirmed 4) follow up with post-incident and RCA
Nguyen T: rollback command queued to infra canary manager. starting rollback for azb only.
Deploy Bot: rollback-request submitted: rollback-id rb-3341 scope=euc2-azb
Ashok P: rollback in progress. pinging infra-team on-call to confirm kernel module reversion.
Eli R: while rollback proceeds, recommend we also increase NLB connection timeout and enable target-group-level deregistration delay to 30s to allow inflight requests to finish and prevent abrupt resets.
Maria K: approved. Nguyen, can you update target-group deregistration-delay?
Nguyen T: updating tg attributes:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30
```
Nguyen T: applied.
Ashok P: rollback completed for azb at 09:18. verification: no duplicate iptables rules present. observing envoy logs: ECONNRESET lines back to baseline.
Eli R: Route53 weight to azb set to 0% (Deploy Bot confirmed) — traffic fully shifted off azb. error rate dropped to normal within 2m.
Deploy Bot: Route53 change completed: status=INSYNC change-id=chg-9087
Maria K: good. I'm going to run a quick canary test hitting euc2 endpoints with synthetic load to validate behavior.
Maria K: canary results: 0.3% errors, p99 latency within normal range. rolling azb targets back slowly.
Nguyen T: re-registering targets with slower rate to avoid flapping. will monitor healthchecks for 10m.
SRE Pager: customer impact final: incident lasted ~18 minutes for most customers, peaked at 20% error rate for impacted subset. tentative severity: SEV2. not a complete outage but significant degradation.
Maria K: handoff to oncall 2 (Eli) for post-incident monitoring and RCA. I’ll open the incident ticket with timeline and link to logs.
Eli R: taking handoff. key action items: RCA writeup (eBPF rollout flagging bug), add pre-deploy verification for ip rule uniqueness, Route53 playbook improvement to speed weighted failover, and a runbook step to drain targets on path duplication detection.
Maria K: assign items and notify infra team. thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
Oncall Bot: Incident channel update: incident-3336543210 created. severity=SEV2, owner=Eli R, status=Monitoring. follow-up due: 2026-03-16T15:00:00Z
